events.text: Utterson accosts Hyde and asks to be admitted to see Jekyll.
events.quote: I thought you might admit me

events.text: Hyde tells Utterson that Dr. Jekyll is from home.
events.quote: You will not find Dr. Jekyll; he is from home

events.text: Utterson asks to see Hyde's face and studies it.
events.quote: Will you let me see your face?

events.text: Hyde gives Utterson his address in Soho.
Hyde angrily accuses Utterson of lying about Jekyll's description.
events.quote: I did not think you would have lied

events.text: Hyde snarls, unlocks the door, and disappears into the house.
events.quote: he had unlocked the door and disappeared into the house

events.text: Utterson walks away deeply disturbed by Hyde's appearance.
Utterson arrives at Jekyll's house and is admitted by Poole.
Poole tells Utterson that Dr. Jekyll has gone out.
Poole confirms Hyde has a key and comes by the dissecting room door.
Poole says all servants have orders to obey Hyde.
events.quote: We have all orders to obey him

events.text: Poole says Hyde never dines there and mostly uses the laboratory.
Utterson goes home fearing Jekyll is in deep waters.
events.quote: my mind misgives me he is in deep waters
